contract.note: Fair. The contract correctly treats the GPT-5 clause as a hedged impression and invents no capability threshold. It assigns no outcome to the whole sentence, and its reliability test for the agent clause (repeatable completion, not perfection) is an ordinary reading.

evidence.note: OpenAI disclosure dated Nov 2023. It describes real-world agents as future work. This is consistent with the claim, but it is a company statement and not an inventory of demonstrations or reliability tests.

OpenAI DevDay disclosure dated Nov 2023. It introduces the Assistants API as a 'first step' toward agent-like experiences. It contains no evidence of repeatable reliable performance, so it neither shows nor rules out a reliable agent demonstration.

reviews.rationale: The sentence pairs a firm historical clause about agents with an explicitly hedged impression about a GPT-5-level model. Under the policy the hedged clause is not scored, and the contract assigns no outcome to the whole record. Even taken alone, the agent clause would be unresolved on this packet: both items are OpenAI disclosures from Nov 2023 that contain no reliability evaluations either way. Neither item confirms or contradicts the claim.
